changes.headline: Joliet's restart awaits confirmation
changes.dek: restart status awaiting public confirmation. Quantum Commodity Intelligence headlines ExxonMobil's Joliet, Illinois refinery back in service as of about Sep 28, but that article is paywalled and no independent non-paywalled confirmation has surfaced. ExxonMobil's last public word (Sep 18) said the refinery was restarting with no date. The ~275 kb/d heavy-crude buyer has been offline since the Sep 13 power outage; Chicago wholesale prices already fell 25-40 cents on the assumption of a restart, not on confirmed rates. While the refinery is offline the Western Canadian Select (WCS) discount to West Texas Intermediate (WTI) stays wide and weak; a confirmed restart is the classic snap-tighter catalyst.
changes.balance_read: If the confirmation lands, ~275 kb/d of WCS demand is back and the discount could narrow quickly in the near-term months. If it does not, the discount stays under pressure.

changes.headline: BP Whiting union talks today
changes.dek: talks reconvene Sep 29. BP Whiting talks with United Steelworkers (USW) Local 7-1 reconvene today (Sep 29). BP called the last session constructive, but the lockout of about 800 workers has been running since Mar 19. BP's other refineries have kept normal operations through the lockout; a walkout at Whiting would cut the single largest PADD 2 demand point for heavy sour crude.
changes.balance_read: A settlement removes the strike wildcard from WCS; a walkout is the mirror image of Joliet — a demand step-off that widens the discount.

changes.headline: Stalled diplomacy lifts crude; the curve says the tightness is near-term
changes.dek: Brent ~$107, WTI ~$94; ~$7.50/mo backwardation. Trump rejected Iran's proposed seven-day Hormuz reopening offer but said the conflict could end soon, and talks continue this week. Monday settled Brent at $105.28 and WTI at $92.60; Tuesday morning trade has Brent near $107 and WTI near $94, a second straight up day. The curve reads acute: about $7.50/month of backwardation between Brent November and December — physical tightness now, normalization further out.
changes.balance_read: Crude is up on stalled diplomacy; the curve says the tightness is near-term. This is flat-price noise for the WCS differential until it changes refinery runs or freight.

changes.headline: Premium moves into freight; Houthi escalation vs Yanbu
changes.dek: inside-Hormuz freight >$22/bbl vs ~$2 a year ago. Hormuz traffic remains 75-90% below pre-conflict levels (UK Maritime Trade Operations, UKMTO), but flows keep healing through expensive ship-to-ship transfers: Middle East exports recovered to about 12.8 million b/d in September, and Saudi September exports are running at more than twice August levels. Freight is doing the work of the war: VLCC rates over $1 million/day and inside-Hormuz freight over $22/bbl vs about $2 a year ago. On the escalation track, the Houthis fired missiles toward Khamis Mushait and drones toward Riyadh over the weekend (all intercepted), claimed attacks on two Saudi tankers in the Red Sea, and France pledged military help defending Yanbu.
changes.balance_read: The Middle East premium has moved into freight: barrels leak out through costly workarounds while Hormuz transits stay suppressed. Houthi escalation keeps Yanbu — the bypass's own terminus — under fire.

changes.headline: Ukraine strikes continue; Putin signs refinery-data decree
changes.dek: Gasoil margins ~$95/bbl; data decree Sep 28. Ukrainian drones hit four fuel facilities in the Krasnodar region overnight, continuing a refining-strike wave into a global distillate market at record stress: Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) gasoil margins near $95/bbl vs a ~$74 August average, and New York Harbor ultra-low-sulfur diesel (NYH ULSD) at a record $113.48 on Sep 16. Separately, Putin signed a Sep 28 decree restricting public access to Russian refinery and export data (volumes, prices, vessels, routes) to complicate Western sanctions enforcement — an official 10-day window exists to define the scope of what goes dark.
changes.balance_read: Distillate-led tightness is constructive for synthetic crude over WCS into winter. The oil read on Putin's decree is the shrinking visibility window on Russian flows, not a price call.

changes.headline: Positioning: WTI crowded long, Brent de-risked
changes.dek: WTI 96th percentile; Brent specs cut ~23%. Speculators in WTI are net long 101,828 contracts (Commodity Futures Trading Commission data), the 96th percentile of the one-year range: a crowded long that would have to unwind if prices fall. In ICE Brent, speculators hold 218,114 net long contracts after cutting about 23% of their longs in a week; that book is already de-risked.
changes.balance_read: A de-escalation headline hurts the crowded WTI longs most; fresh escalation could drive a WTI catch-up rally, since WTI lags Brent by about $11.9.

changes.headline: Commercial shorts build on the Canadian differentials
changes.dek: -5,874 lots (WCS); -2,259 lots (SW). Our Commitments of Traders (COT) model flags high-confidence commercial-sized net-short builds on the ICE WCS 1A and ICE SW 1A differentials: 5,874 lots on WCS, 2,259 on SW. That fits trade houses hedging export economics or producers selling into the rally ahead of Joliet's return. Probable, never fact.
changes.balance_read: Trade houses and producers look to be hedging the Canadian differentials into Joliet's return, but that attribution is inferred, not confirmed.

changes.headline: Trans Mountain toll deal approved; Mainline apportioned
changes.dek: TMX 90% contractible; October apportionment 8%/4%. The Canada Energy Regulator (CER) approved Trans Mountain's negotiated toll settlement Monday, ending an 18-month dispute; up to 90% of 890 kb/d can now be contracted firm, with the optimization program targeting 1.19 MMb/d by late 2028. Near-term, Enbridge's October Mainline apportionment (official notice, Sep 16) is binding: 8% on Line 2/93 lights and 4% on Line 4/67/93 heavies at Kerrobert, plus 7% on Line 1 refined volumes at Regina (FPA) and 3% at Kerrobert (SPA). CER June data: Keystone at 94% of available capacity, Mainline excluding Gretna at 94.5%; implied spare takeaway about 272 kb/d.
changes.balance_read: Medium-term egress certainty: the contractible share of Trans Mountain rises from 80% to 90% of 890 kb/d. Near-term, Mainline apportionment binds: extra barrels clear through price (wider differentials, deeper cuts), not through spare capacity.
changes.publishers: CER decision; Enbridge Connecting Pipelines notice

changes.headline: Merey discounts widen on record freight; 7th tanker seized
changes.dek: Merey offers -$18/-$20 vs Brent; freight ~$3.5M per voyage. Venezuelan Merey is being offered at $18-20/bbl under Brent into the US and Europe, with traders seeking steeper discounts as tanker costs squeeze margins: Jose-to-USGC Aframax freight is near $3.5 million per voyage (~$5-7/bbl equivalent). US imports of Venezuelan crude ran 583 kb/d in the week ending Sep 18, down from 782. US Southern Command seized the sanctioned aframax Sagitta, the seventh tanker seizure under the blockade regime; about 20% of Venezuelan seaborne exports are moving into Caribbean storage in the Bahamas, Curacao and Saint Lucia, marketed by Vitol and Trafigura. Destination splits remain estimates: dark-fleet gaps and ship-to-ship transfers make exact shares unverifiable.
changes.balance_read: High freight is bearish WCS, not a moat: distressed heavy-sour length either prices down to clear against WCS or goes to storage as overhang.
changes.publishers: Reuters-linked reporting; EIA weekly petroleum status

changes.headline: Blending arb window open (illustrative)
changes.dek: modeled net incentive $5.51/bbl. Our blender-behavior nowcast (in-house, synthetic assumptions clearly flagged) has the heavy-into-light arbitrage window open: the viscosity constraint is binding and the incentive to blend heavy barrels into the light pool reads a net $5.51/bbl on the modeled stack, or about 43.2 kb/d of reclassification per 100 kb/d of light tendered. Direction matters, level does not.
changes.balance_read: An illustrative model read, not a live market print: while the window is open, barrels reclassify from the heavy pool into the light pool at the margin — a softener on the discount, not a directional call.

flags.title: Synthetic crude (SCO) supply returns ~Oct 5 to mid-Oct
flags.detail: Syncrude's 50-day coker turnaround wraps around Oct 5 and CNRL's Horizon upgrader turnaround ends around mid-October. Both restore synthetic-crude supply, which should narrow the synthetic-crude premium over WCS into the fall. Trigger: Confirmed completion dates on either turnaround move this into the ranked changes.

flags.title: Joliet restart awaiting confirmation
flags.detail: Quantum Commodity Intelligence headlines Joliet back in service as of about Sep 28, but the article is paywalled and no public confirmation exists. ExxonMobil's last public statement (Sep 18): power restored, restart underway, no date given. The confirmation itself is the catalyst: the discount snaps tighter when it lands, stays under pressure while it does not. Trigger: Public confirmation from ExxonMobil or a second source turns this into the top ranked change.
